title: Install without the CI reuse recipes

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: custom-adapter integrated state

**Verdict: Caught.** The maintained assertion `ci-integrated-state-custom.test.mjs:52` ("B must have integrated-state evidence from C", in test "declared policy: custom C green with E pending completes accepted B as validated C outside the startup stream") failed after the fault. The product had judged accepted B `unresolved` instead of `success` from the custom adapter's same-target green descendant C. This claim covers only that path: the custom `ciAdapter` (test-owned `ci-custom-command-adapter.mjs`) feeding integrated-state judgement through `currentCommandAttempt`.

**Next proof action:** none for this promise. The maintained journey catches this fault.

## Revision checked
- Story: `.planning/seeds/SEED-423-shrink-the-installed-distribution.md#install-without-ci-reuse-recipes`. Plan: `.planning/slice-plans/792-install-without-ci-reuse-recipes/PLAN.md`.
- Revision: `d516ab3ebac31265c991f9b88fb8cf57f125c1e0`, checked in an isolated detached scratch worktree (`git worktree add --detach`). The worktree was clean before the probe (0 changed paths) and had `npm ci` run. Node v24.21.0.

## Promise
"The integrated-state journey with a custom CI command adapter still passes, now against its test-owned adapter." Expected behavior: when a custom adapter reports a successful current attempt of the declared check/context on the same target branch at a descendant C, accepted B completes from integrated-state evidence validated at C.

## Fault
- Location: `Distribution/src/skills/dough-execute-plan/scripts/ci-command-attempts.mjs`, `currentCommandAttempt`. This is the custom-adapter-only current-attempt reader that `ci-command-adapter.mjs` `readCurrentAttempt` uses.
- Change: `headBranch: providerBranch,` became `headBranch: facts.providerBranch,`. This is a plausible destructuring slip. `providerBranch` was already removed from `facts`, so the custom adapter's current attempt never names its target. As a result, a later same-target successful snapshot no longer counts.
- Revision of the caller's suggestion: the caller suggested faulting the shared `ci-integrated-state*.mjs`. I faulted the custom adapter's own integrated-state fact path instead. That path is specific to the custom `ciAdapter` route whose proof moved in this story, whereas the shared judge is also exercised by the GitHub journeys. The fault still matches the caller's suggested kind: a later same-target successful snapshot does not count.
- No fixtures or assertions were changed.

## Commands
From the scratch checkout:
`env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_CASE_OUTCOMES=<file> OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_TIMES=<file> caffeinate -s -i bash scripts/test.sh Distribution/tests/skills/dough-execute-plan/ci-integrated-state-custom.test.mjs Distribution/tests/skills/dough-execute-plan/ci-integrated-state-journey.test.mjs`

The runner prints nothing on success, so I added the case-outcome file to record that the cases actually ran.

## Observations
- **Baseline:** exit 0. All 6 custom cases and all 4 journey cases passed.
- **Reach:** the custom test builds its provider with `customProvider(shape)`. That provider installs `ciAdapter: [node, wrapper]` over the test-owned `ci-custom-command-adapter.mjs`, so the product's `createCommandAcquisition` → `readCurrentAttempt` → `currentCommandAttempt` path runs. The GitHub-provider journey file `ci-integrated-state-journey.test.mjs` does not reach this code and stayed green (4/4) under the fault, as expected.
- **Independent wrong-behavior witness:** a scratch Node script, run outside the maintained tests, called the product's `answeredCommandAttempts` → `currentCommandAttempt` → `currentAttemptIneligibility`. It used a same-target (`main`) successful `project-checks`/`push` attempt at C.
  - Under the fault: `{"ineligibility":"different_target"}` with `headBranch` absent, so C cannot validate B.
  - After restoration: `{"headBranch":"main","ineligibility":"eligible"}`.
- **Faulted run:** exit 1. Three custom cases failed.
  - "declared policy: custom C green with E pending completes accepted B as validated C…" failed at `ci-integrated-state-custom.test.mjs:52`: `actual: 'unresolved', expected: 'success'`, message "B must have integrated-state evidence from C". **This is the catching assertion.**
  - "C's newer rerun, pending and then failed, contradicts its older green…" failed in the earlier `journey.awaitCoverage(... integrated?.state === "success", "C's green")` helper. The observer worker exited with `budget_expired` before C's green was recognized.
  - "unavailable discovery withdraws C's retained green and never completes B" failed the same way, also in the `awaitCoverage` "C's green" wait.
  - The other 3 custom cases passed (another-branch, legacy exact, legacy-with-policy). The 4 journey cases passed.
  - The two later failures ran into the 60 s observation budget, which is why the custom file took 135.8 s.
- **Restoration:** I restored the file with `git checkout -- <file>` under an EXIT/INT/TERM trap. After that, `git status --short` showed 0 changed paths and HEAD was still `d516ab3eb…`. The same command then exited 0 with 6/6 custom and 4/4 journey cases passing. The scratch worktree was then removed.
- **Not probed:** the caller's secondary install-absence check (`execution-payload-update.sh` find for `*reuse*`). This skill runs one check per invocation, so that one has no verdict here.
- **Load:** the 1-minute load average was about 8.7–10.3 during the runs. No baseline or restored flake was observed.
- **Prior dispositions:** none known that this evidence matches. This check makes no new repair decision.

## Costs
- **Test runtime:** measured from the runner's per-job seconds, for the custom and journey files respectively.
  - Baseline: 24.1 s and 23.0 s.
  - Faulted: 135.8 s and 17.9 s.
  - Restored: 12.2 s and 11.5 s.
  - An earlier silent baseline run took 12.9 s wall (measured with `time`).
- **Human effort:** unavailable. There was no human involvement to measure; the check ran unattended as a subagent.
- **Agent effort:** unavailable. There is no separately supported token or turn measure accessible from inside this run.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 286032 ms (measured), from 1795424636942 to 1795424922974 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision d516ab3ebac31265c991f9b88fb8cf57f125c1e0: Caught; no follow-up.
